mainTopic: A wife's clothing and intimacy rights, her funeral and burial costs, and the court supporting the family of an insane or absent husband
overview: The amud opens with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who reads the words of the פסוק (שמות 21:10) as rules about a wife's clothing: the clothes must fit her age and the season. רב יוסף then teaches a ברייתא that reads שְׁאֵרָהּ as closeness of body during intimacy, which supports רב הונא's ruling about a husband who insists on staying clothed. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's argument over funeral flutes and a mourning woman. תנא קמא holds that a wife shares her husband's higher status only while alive. רבי יהודה holds that she shares it even after death, and the הלכה follows him. The גמרא then discusses how the בית דין uses an insane man's property to support his family, and why that differs from a man who went overseas. It also explains what 'something else' (jewelry or charity) means. It adds that an absent husband's wife is buried at least by his dignity. It ends by teaching that a man cannot order that his own burial not be paid from his property. Finally a new משנה begins about a daughter staying under her father's authority.

steps.title: Reading all three words of the פסוק as rules about clothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב links שְׁאֵרָהּ to כְּסוּתָהּ, and כְּסוּתָהּ to עוֹנָתָהּ. The clothing must fit her age and the season.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: 'Her flesh, her clothing' means: give her clothing that fits her body, meaning her age. He shouldn't give a young girl's clothes to an older woman, or an older woman's clothes to a young girl. 'Her clothing and her time' means: give her clothing that fits the time of year. He shouldn't give new, heavy clothes in summer, or worn-out clothes in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב explains the three words of the פסוק so that all of them are about one thing: the clothes a husband must give his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He pairs the words. שְׁאֵרָהּ tells us how to choose her כְּסוּתָהּ: by her age. עוֹנָתָהּ also tells us how to choose her כְּסוּתָהּ: by the season. So in his reading, עוֹנָה here means a season of the year, not marital relations.

keyTerms.meaning: Her flesh; here, her body and age
Her time; here, the season of the year

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read עוֹנָתָהּ here as marital relations. In this view it means a season of the year, and it tells us what kind of clothes to give.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
'Her flesh, her clothing' —
according to her flesh, give her clothing,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יִתֵּן לָהּ לֹא שֶׁל יַלְדָּה לִזְקֵינָהּ,
phrases.english: that he should not give her a young girl's clothes for an older woman,
nor an older woman's clothes for a young girl.
'Her clothing and her time' —
according to her time (season), give her clothing,
that he should not give new (heavy) clothes in the summer days,
nor worn-out clothes in the rainy days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reading of the פסוק, continuing the ברייתא from before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The clothing a husband gives must suit his wife's age and the season of the year.

steps.title: רב יוסף: שְׁאֵרָהּ means closeness of body
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches a ברייתא that reads שְׁאֵרָהּ as closeness of flesh during intimacy. The husband may not act like the Persians, who had relations while dressed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: 'Her flesh' means closeness of body. He must not treat her the way the Persians did, who had relations in their clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא with a different reading of שְׁאֵרָהּ. In this reading it is about physical closeness between husband and wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב read שְׁאֵרָהּ as a guide for choosing clothes. This ברייתא reads it as its own obligation: real body-to-body closeness. That rules out relations while both are dressed.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
'Her flesh' — this is closeness of flesh,
that he should not treat her in the manner of the Persians,
who use their beds in their clothes.
phrases.notes: 'Use their beds' is a polite way of saying they have relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the word שְׁאֵרָהּ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שְׁאֵרָהּ requires real physical closeness during relations, not relations while clothed.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's ברייתא supports רב הונא. רב הונא rules that a husband who insists on relations only while both are clothed must divorce his wife and pay her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב הונא, who said: if a man says, 'I only want relations if I'm in my clothes and she's in hers,' he must divorce her and pay her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב יוסף's ברייתא backs up a ruling of רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה requires closeness of flesh, then refusing it means refusing a real obligation. That is why רב הונא can force the husband to divorce her and pay the כתובה. The ברייתא gives רב הונא's ruling a source in a פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a practical rule: a husband cannot set this condition on his wife.

phrases.english: This supports Rav Huna,
for Rav Huna said:
One who says: 'I do not want
except that I am in my clothes and she is in her clothes' —
he must divorce her and give her the כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא as support for an אמורא's ruling
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that a husband who insists on staying clothed must divorce and pay the כתובה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's ברייתא reading שְׁאֵרָהּ as closeness of flesh
steps.whatToRemember: On this amud the פסוק's words get two readings: clothing by age and season (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב), and closeness of flesh (רב יוסף's ברייתא), which supports רב הונא.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה and inferring the view of תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה: even the poorest man must provide funeral flutes and a mourning woman. From this it infers that תנא קמא holds a husband is not required to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says רבי יהודה holds: even the poorest man in Israel must provide (two flutes and a mourning woman). That shows תנא קמא holds these are not required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic in the משנה. It quotes רבי יהודה and draws out what the first opinion must hold, to set up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says 'even the poorest.' That word 'even' shows he is adding something that תנא קמא did not require. So the two views disagree about whether these funeral items are part of what a husband owes.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even the poorest man in Israel, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה: he must provide at least two flutes and a mourning woman for his wife's funeral.

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר הָנֵי לָא.
phrases.english: By inference, the first tanna holds these are not required.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ עָנִי שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה requires funeral flutes and a mourning woman even from a poor husband; תנא קמא does not.

steps.title: What case are they arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact case. If this is her family's custom, why would תנא קמא excuse him? If it isn't her family's custom, why would רבי יהודה require it?
steps.simpleTranslation: What's the case? If it's her custom, what is the reason of תנא קמא, who says he doesn't have to? And if it's not her custom, what is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that each simple version of the case makes one of the two opinions hard to understand. It is pushing for the real case they argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her family usually has these at funerals, leaving them out would shame her, so תנא קמא's ruling seems wrong. If her family doesn't do this, there's no reason to require it, so רבי יהודה's ruling seems wrong. Neither choice fits both opinions.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If it is her way (her family's custom) —

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא דְּאָמַר לָא?
phrases.english: what is the reason of the first tanna, who says he need not?
And if it is not her way —
what is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the dispute that was just inferred
steps.kashyaTarget: The dispute between תנא קמא and רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible cases (her custom or not her custom) leave one of the two opinions without a reason.

steps.title: The case: his family's custom, not hers
steps.stepSummary: They argue where this is his family's custom but not hers. תנא קמא holds that 'she rises with him' applies only during life, not after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is needed where this is his family's custom but not hers. תנא קמא holds: when we say a wife rises with her husband and does not go down with him, that applies only while she is alive, but not after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by finding a middle case: the custom belongs to his family, not hers. It then explains תנא קמא's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a wife gets to share her husband's higher standard of living ('rises with him'). תנא קמא says this rule holds only during her lifetime. So at her funeral he only has to follow her own family's custom. The next step gives רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case
She rises with him (to his higher status)
She does not go down with him

steps.confusionAlert: 'Rises with him' means she shares his higher standard of living. It does not mean she loses her own status if his is lower.

phrases.english: No, it is needed:
for example, where it is his own way (custom)
but not her own way,
the first tanna holds:
when we say she rises with him
and does not go down with him —
that applies during life,
but after death — not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by defining a middle case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a third case that neither side of the question covered
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case must be either her custom or not her custom, and either way one opinion has no reason
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is his custom but not hers; תנא קמא limits 'she rises with him' to her lifetime
steps.whatToRemember: The dispute is about a custom of the husband's family only. תנא קמא: the wife shares his status only during life.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's side: even after death
steps.stepSummary: Completing the answer from step 6: רבי יהודה holds that 'she rises with him' applies even after her death.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה holds: even after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it started in step 6 by giving רבי יהודה's side of the argument. He says the wife keeps her husband's status even after she dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 we learned that תנא קמא limits 'she rises with him' to her lifetime. רבי יהודה disagrees: the rule continues after death too. So if the husband's family uses flutes and mourning women at funerals, he must give her the same.

keyTerms.meaning: 'She rises with him': a wife shares her husband's higher standard of living

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
Even after death.
phrases.notes: He means: she keeps her husband's status even after she dies, so he must pay for a funeral that fits his family's custom.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: אֲפִילּוּ לְאַחַר מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided answer begun in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both sides argue in the same case (his family's custom, not hers) and differ on whether 'she rises with him' continues after death
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed there was no case where both opinions make sense
steps.terutzMaskana: תנא קמא: only during life; רבי יהודה: even after death

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes מר עוקבא: the הלכה is like רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא: the הלכה is like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the funeral argument. We follow רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, a husband must honor his wife at her funeral according to his own family's custom, even though it is not her family's custom. Her right to share his status does not end when she dies.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...
An early אמורא, often quoted by רב חסדא

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is like רבי יהודה: a wife shares her husband's status even after death, so he pays for a funeral fitting his family's custom.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said that Mar Ukva said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument explained in steps 6-7
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A wife rises with her husband even after death; the halacha follows רבי יהודה

steps.title: Supporting the family of a man who became insane
steps.stepSummary: Another ruling by רב חסדא in the name of מר עוקבא: when a man becomes insane, the court uses his property to support his wife, sons, daughters, and 'something else.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא also said in the name of מר עוקבא: if a man becomes insane, the בית דין goes into his property and supports his wife, his sons and his daughters, and also gives 'something else.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just quoted רב חסדא in the name of מר עוקבא, it now brings another ruling of theirs. This one is about a man who lost his sanity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man cannot manage his own money, so the בית דין steps in. It supports not only his wife but also his children, plus an extra item called 'something else,' which the גמרא explains in steps 12–14.

keyTerms.meaning: The court 'goes down' into his property, taking control of it to pay for needs
'Something else': an extra item, explained later

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said that Mar Ukva said:
One who became insane —
the court goes down into his property
and feeds and provides a livelihood for his wife,
and his sons and his daughters, and something else.
phrases.notes: Hold on to 'something else'; the גמרא explains it in step 13.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא: מִי שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brought because it is another ruling with the same chain of names (רב חסדא from מר עוקבא)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an insane man, the court supports his wife, sons, daughters, and 'something else' from his property

steps.title: רבינא's challenge from the man who went overseas
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי: a ברייתא says that for a man who went overseas, the court supports only his wife, not his children and not 'something else.' Why is the insane man different?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: How is this different from the ברייתא that says: if a man went overseas and his wife asks for food, the court goes into his property and supports his wife, but not his sons and daughters, and not 'something else'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the ruling about the insane man. He points to a ברייתא about an absent husband where the court gives much less.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the husband is not around to take care of his family. Yet the ברייתא supports only the wife, while מר עוקבא's ruling also supports the children and 'something else.' רבינא wants to know what makes the two cases different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (a challenge comparing two cases)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
What is different from that which is taught in a baraita:
One who went overseas
and his wife claims sustenance —
the court goes down into his property,
and feeds and provides a livelihood for his wife,
but not his sons and daughters,
and not something else?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 9 using a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: מר עוקבא's ruling that the court supports an insane man's children and 'something else'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A similar case (absent husband) gives only the wife support, so why should the insane man's case give more?

steps.title: Leaving by choice versus not by choice
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers: a man who left knowingly is different from one who 'left' his responsibilities without knowing (by becoming insane).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Don't you see a difference between someone who leaves knowingly and someone who leaves without knowing?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא's challenge by showing the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man who went overseas chose to leave, and he could have left money for his children; since he didn't, we assume he did not want to. The insane man never chose to stop caring for his family, so we assume he would want them supported from his property.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't there a difference for you? (a way of saying 'obviously these differ')

steps.whatToRemember: The insane man's family gets more support than the overseas man's family, because the insane man did not choose to leave them.

phrases.english: He said to him: And is there no difference for you
between one who leaves knowingly
and one who leaves unknowingly?
phrases.notes: The one who 'leaves unknowingly' is the insane man; he didn't decide to drop his responsibilities.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא שָׁאנֵי לָךְ בֵּין יוֹצֵא לְדַעַת לַיּוֹצֵא שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An absent husband and an insane husband seem alike, so the support should be the same
steps.terutzMaskana: Leaving by choice shows he didn't want to support them; insanity was not his choice, so we assume he would want to

steps.title: What is 'something else'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'something else' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'something else'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unclear phrase 'something else' used in the rulings above. This sets up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the insane-man ruling and the ברייתא mention 'something else' without saying what it is. The גמרא now wants to define it.

phrases.english: What is 'something else'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to explain a term from steps 9-10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase 'something else'

steps.title: Jewelry or charity
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says 'something else' is jewelry; רב יוסף says it is charity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: it is jewelry. רב יוסף said: it is charity.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different answers to what 'something else' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חסדא, 'something else' is the wife's jewelry. According to רב יוסף, it is money given to צדקה from the husband's property.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said: This is ornaments.
Rav Yosef said: Charity.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: זֶה תַּכְשִׁיט. רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: צְדָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב חסדא: jewelry; רב יוסף: charity

steps.title: What each view means in practice
steps.stepSummary: If 'something else' is jewelry, then charity is surely not given either. If it is charity, jewelry is still given, since the husband does not want his wife to look shabby.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says jewelry: all the more so charity is not given. The one who says charity: but jewelry we do give her, because he doesn't want her to be shamed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the two opinions differ in practice, focusing on the overseas case where 'something else' is not given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא: if the court won't even give her jewelry, it surely won't give away his money to צדקה. רב יוסף: only צדקה is held back, but jewelry is given, because a husband doesn't want his wife to look poor and embarrassed. So the real difference is whether the wife of an absent husband gets jewelry.

keyTerms.meaning: He is pleased with it, it suits him
She would be shamed, look shabby

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'not given' talks about the overseas case. In the insane man's case, 'something else' IS given, whichever meaning you take.
steps.whatToRemember: All agree charity is not given from an absent husband's property; they argue only about jewelry.

phrases.english: The one who says ornaments,
all the more so charity.
The one who says charity,
but ornaments we do give her,
because it is not pleasing to him that she be demeaned.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר תַּכְשִׁיט, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן צְדָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the practical difference between the two answers in step 13
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Charity is not given from an absent husband's property according to both; jewelry is given according to רב יוסף but not according to רב חסדא

steps.title: The court buries the wife of an absent husband from his property
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין, quoting רב הונא, rules that if a husband is overseas and his wife dies, the court goes into his property and buries her according to his dignity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רב הונא: If a man went overseas and his wife died, the court goes into his property and buries her according to his honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling. When the husband is away, the court uses his money to pay for his wife's burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burying his wife is one of the husband's duties, so being away does not cancel it. The court acts for him and takes the money from his property. The words 'according to his dignity' will be questioned right away.

keyTerms.meaning: They go into his property, meaning the court takes money from his assets
According to his honor or social status

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin said that Rav Huna said:
One who went overseas
and his wife died —
the court goes into his property,
and buries her according to his dignity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the court using an absent husband's property for his wife, from steps 10-14, and moves on to burial.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the husband is overseas, the court pays for his dead wife's burial from his property, according to his dignity.

steps.title: Why his dignity and not hers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording: why should the burial follow the husband's dignity and not the wife's?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to his dignity and not according to hers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the word 'his' in the ruling. If she came from a more important family, shouldn't she be buried by her own higher standard?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, the ruling seems to say only the husband's status counts. That would hurt a wife who came from a higher family. The question pushes the גמרא to explain the wording.

phrases.english: According to his dignity and not according to her dignity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ruling in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'לפי כבודו' in רב הונא's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the wife's family was more honored, limiting her burial to the husband's level seems wrong.

steps.title: Read it as 'even according to his dignity'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ruling means 'even according to his dignity.' If he is the more honored one, she is buried by his higher standard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: even according to his dignity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the words differently. It does not mean 'only his dignity,' but 'also his dignity, if it is higher.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, her own status is never taken away. The ruling adds that if the husband's status is higher, she gets his level. So she gets whichever standard is higher.

phrases.english: Say: even according to his dignity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed to limit her to his status alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means she is buried even by his higher status, and never below her own.

steps.title: She rises with him and does not go down, even after death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the lesson: a wife rises to her husband's status and does not drop to a lower one, and this holds even after her death.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us: she goes up with him and does not go down with him, even after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new lesson inside רב הונא's ruling. The rule that a wife rises with her husband applies even to her burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the marriage a wife shares her husband's higher status but keeps her own if his is lower. רב הונא's ruling shows that death does not end this: even when the בית דין buries her for an absent husband, her burial follows the higher status. This matches רבי יהודה in the משנה (steps 7–8), whom the הלכה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
She rises with him to his status
She does not go down with him to a lower status

steps.whatToRemember: A wife gets the higher of the two statuses, hers or her husband's, and this applies even to her burial.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the husband's duty to honor his wife continues past her death, so her burial must match the higher status.

phrases.english: This teaches us:
she rises with him and does not go down with him,
and even after death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the lesson that the reading in step 17 shows.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rule that a wife rises with her husband and does not go down applies even to her burial after death.

steps.title: A man who says 'don't bury her from my property' is listened to
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה rules that if a man says, 'If she dies, do not bury her from my property,' the court listens to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: If someone says, 'If she dies, do not bury her from his property,' we listen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב מתנה about a man who orders that his property not be used to bury his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance, the ruling says the man's instruction works and the court follows it. The next step asks why his words should make any difference.

keyTerms.meaning: We listen to him, we follow his instructions

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said: One who says:
'If she dies, do not bury her from his property' —
we listen to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching on burial costs, next to רב הונא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man's order not to bury his wife from his property is followed.

steps.title: His words add nothing, since the property belongs to the orphans anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference his statement makes. If the reason is that the property has passed to the orphans, that is true even when he says nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different when he says it? That the property has fallen before the orphans? Even when he does not say it, the property lies before the orphans!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מתנה's ruling. It argues that the man's statement changes nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason his money would not be used for her burial is that it already belongs to the orphans, his heirs. But that is true whether or not he says anything. So the ruling, as stated, teaches nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The property has fallen before the orphans, meaning it passed to his heirs

phrases.english: What is different when he says it?
That the property has fallen before the orphans.
Even when he does not say it,
the property lies before the orphans!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מתנה's ruling that we listen to the man.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason works the same whether or not he speaks, so his statement adds nothing and the ruling is pointless.

steps.title: Changed case: a man who says not to bury himself from his property is ignored
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes רב מתנה's teaching. If a man says, 'If I die, do not bury me from my property,' we do not listen, because he cannot make his sons richer and push his burial costs onto the community.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: One who says, 'If he dies, do not bury him from his property,' we do not listen to him. It is not in his power to make his sons rich and throw himself onto the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by retelling רב מתנה's teaching as a different case. The man is talking about his own burial, and here the court ignores him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If his own money is not used, the community would have to pay for his burial out of charity, while his sons keep the money. A man does not have the right to arrange that. So the court uses his property anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, the teaching must be told differently
We do not listen to him
It is not in his power
Throw himself onto the community, making it pay for him

steps.whatToRemember: A man cannot order that his own burial not be paid from his property. Doing so would leave the bill to the community while his heirs keep the money.
steps.confusionAlert: The final ruling is the opposite of the first version: 'שומעין לו' (we listen) becomes 'אין שומעין לו' (we do not listen), and the case is now about his own burial, not his wife's.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a person's own burial is a cost on his estate, and he cannot shift it onto charity for his heirs' benefit.

phrases.english: Rather: One who says:
'If he dies, do not bury him from his property' —
we do not listen to him.

phrases.aramaic: לָאו כׇּל הֵימֶנּוּ שֶׁיַּעֲשִׁיר אֶת בָּנָיו
phrases.english: It is not in his power to make his sons rich
and throw himself onto the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הָאוֹמֵר: אִם מֵת הוּא, לֹא תִּקְבְּרוּהוּ מִנְּכָסָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by changing the case of רב מתנה's teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retelling the teaching with a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב מתנה was talking about the wife's burial and said we listen to the husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב מתנה was talking about the man's own burial and said we do not listen, because he cannot push his burial costs onto the community to enrich his sons.

steps.title: A daughter stays under her father's authority until she enters
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. It states that a daughter is always in her father's רשות until she 'enters.' The rest of the sentence comes in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: She is always under her father's authority until she enters...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's discussion is over, and a new משנה begins with a basic rule: a daughter stays under her father's רשות until a certain point. This line sets up the rest of the sentence, which tells us what she enters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לעולם, 'always,' stresses that the father's authority does not end early. It lasts even after אירוסין. The cutoff point is 'until she enters,' so her status depends on a real change of place, not only on the act of betrothal.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה text.
Always. Here it stresses that the father's authority continues the whole time.
The father's authority or domain over his daughter.
Until she enters. This marks the point where the father's authority ends.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume אירוסין alone takes a girl out of her father's רשות. The word 'always' teaches that she stays under him until she 'enters.'

phrases.english: MISHNA:
She is always under her father's authority
until she enters

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ לְעוֹלָם הִיא בִּרְשׁוּת הָאָב עַד שֶׁתִּכָּנֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of a husband's burial duties ended in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A daughter stays in her father's רשות, even after אירוסין, until she enters the next stage. That stage is finished in the next line.
